title.title: An area law for two-dimensional gapped systems
title.subtitle: Claim: a uniform global gap bounds each region's entanglement entropy by a constant times its boundary

object.caption: $S(A) \le C\,|\partial A|$: entropy bounded by boundary edges, not cells

beats.text: A gapped Hamiltonian on a patch of $\mathbb Z^2$, and a region $A$ of its ground state
Volume law: entropy grows with the cells of $A$. Area law: with its boundary edges
Claim: a global spectral gap alone forces the area law, for any region shape

achievement.label: Area-law conjecture for 2D gapped ground states
achievement.context: Before: 1D (Hastings 2007); in 2D only frustration-free systems with local gaps (STOC 2022)
achievement.note: PEPS companion: bond dimension poly($L$), error $\le 1/L$, existence only

verify.ourCheck: We read the papers' claims and caveats; we did not referee them

sources.quote: Proven in 1D by Hastings (J. Stat. Mech. 2007, P08024)

sources.ref: article, An area law for two-dimensional gapped systems

plain: Entanglement in a calm 2D quantum material grows with a region's fence, not its field: border, not area

steps: Use only the energy gap to build approximate ground-state filters
Organize them layer by layer across the square lattice
Turn them into an entanglement bound set by the boundary

voice.text: An area law in two dimensions.
Entanglement of a region: does it grow with its area, or only with its boundary?
From the gap alone, build ground-state filters layer by layer and bound entanglement.
Claimed: the boundary wins, for any region.
